stemBlocks.value: A diagram shows line segment AB with A(−4, −1) and B(2, 7). (a) Calculate the length AB. (b) Determine the coordinates of the midpoint of AB.
Think first: Read the two endpoints off the grid first, then the length and midpoint are both formula work.

contentBlocks.value: A is below the x-axis at the left, B is up and to the right

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the horizontal and vertical changes.

contentBlocks.value: Result: Change of 6 across and 8 up

solutionSteps.instruction: Average the x-coordinates for the midpoint.

strategyBlocks.value: Read A and B from the diagram, apply the distance formula √((x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²) for the length, then average the coordinates for the midpoint.

whyThisWorks.value: The distance formula is Pythagoras' theorem applied to the right-angled triangle whose legs are the horizontal and vertical changes between the two points. Squaring removes any negative signs, so the length never depends on which point you call first — unlike the gradient, where order controls the sign. The midpoint averages each coordinate because halfway across and halfway up locates the centre of the segment.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting to square root at the end and giving 100 as the length.
